title: telemetry.jsonl event record (TECH_SPEC §3.4 envelope + §8.1 payloads, ADR-008 event vocabulary)
description: One object per line of ledger/telemetry.jsonl. Common envelope on every event (ts, run_id, domain, tool, event); event-specific payload by `event`. metrics_scan.py (§8.2) derives every metric from these rows — no metric is hand-entered. Post-ADR-008 the `stage` vocabulary is the pivot pipeline (ingest → si_v1 → enrichment → si_v2 → jira) and three enrichment events join the nine originals (`verdict`, `escalation`, `disposition` — TECH_SPEC banner §3.4–3.6, D-A5/6/8/9/16/17). NOTE: the ledger records THAT things happened, never artifact CONTENT (FR-XS-05) — a finding is referenced by `finding_id` into enrichment.json, never inlined; the operator's rationale lives in decisions.jsonl.

stage.description: The ADR-008 pipeline stages. `ingest` covers the whole Data & context layer including the code-lane map build (it is the code lane of the source_processor fan-out, not a separate operator stage); `enrichment` is the two arms + the disposition walkthrough; `si_v2` is the apply pass that writes v2; `jira` covers plan authoring and the push. Old BRD/FRD-era names (brd_authoring, frd_authoring, code_map, code_impact, jira_authoring, jira_push) are RETIRED and rejected here.

arm.description: Which enrichment arm produced the finding (D-A8). `impact` = Arm 1, requirement → code (the `code_impact` role, per-assertion impact + closure). `claim` = Arm 2, claim → code (the `claim_verifier` role, point lookup then stop).

verdict.description: The outcome of resolving one assertion/claim against the code map (D-A5/D-A8). `confirmed` = code agrees; `contradicted` = code disagrees; `answered` = code closes an unsourced [TBD] (D-A6 row 3); `impacted` = Arm 1 found a derived impact; `no_code_found` = Arm 1 found no implementation for a requirement (the four-way ambiguous gap, D-A16); `unverifiable` = no match anywhere — usually a partner/upstream system, itself worth surfacing (D-A8).

route.description: Where the finding went WITHOUT a human (D-A16's routing table). `auto_correct` = in-place correction of a source-derived claim; `auto_fill` = a [TBD] gap closed; `auto_write` = a technical-consequence impact written to its section; `escalate` = ambiguous / scope-moving / would overrule a human — goes to the walkthrough, never auto-applied; `none` = nothing to do (a confirmed claim). M12 enrichment yield = the auto_correct + auto_write + auto_fill counts.

escalation_reason.description: Why the finding needs a human (the four D-A16 escalation triggers). `operator_contradiction` = code contradicts an operator answer or the UI_INPUT frame; `business_visible` = a derived impact someone must decide about (D-A9); `no_code_found` = the four-way gap; `scope_moving` = anything that changes scope (operator-decided, always).

call.description: The operator's call at the disposition walkthrough (D-A16/D-A17) — the FINDING disposition, NOT the D-A12 source disposition (that one classifies an input artifact and lives in UI_INPUT/index.json). `accept` = the finding stands as proposed; `reject` = it was wrong (an Arm 1 search miss) → dropped; `reroute` = real, but it lands somewhere other than proposed (§7/§8/§12/§14); `defer` = cannot determine yet → becomes a §17 open question. The defer path is REQUIRED: without it the walkthrough pressures people into fabricating certainty.
